mechanism: Concurrent PDE5 inhibition and nitrate therapy produces profound systemic vasodilation and life-threatening hypotension.
management: Coadministration is strictly contraindicated. Maintain at least a 24-hour nitrate-free interval before PDE5 inhibitor use.

mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition by clarithromycin significantly increases simvastatin exposure raising risk of rhabdomyolysis.
management: Combination is contraindicated. Suspend simvastatin during clarithromycin therapy or switch to a non-CYP3A4 antibiotic.

mechanism: Antiplatelet effect of aspirin combines with anticoagulant effect of warfarin markedly increasing gastrointestinal bleeding risk.
management: Avoid concurrent use unless clinically indicated. Monitor INR closely and assess for signs of active bleeding.

mechanism: Ibuprofen causes platelet inhibition and gastric mucosal injury synergistically elevating major hemorrhage risk with warfarin.
management: Avoid co-prescription. Use paracetamol for analgesia or monitor INR and hemoglobin frequently if co-administered.

mechanism: Diclofenac inhibits COX-1 dependent platelet aggregation and may displace warfarin from protein binding heightening bleed risk.
management: Avoid concurrent therapy. Consider safer analgesic alternatives such as paracetamol and monitor anticoagulant response.

mechanism: Metronidazole inhibits CYP2C9 metabolism of S-warfarin causing sharp elevation in warfarin plasma levels and INR prolongation.
management: Reduce warfarin dosage by 30-50% upon starting metronidazole. Monitor INR every 2 to 3 days during antimicrobial therapy.

mechanism: Dual systemic NSAID therapy provides no additive analgesic efficacy while drastically increasing gastrointestinal ulceration risk.
management: Discontinue one NSAID immediately. Dual oral NSAID therapy is inappropriate and should be avoided.

mechanism: Omeprazole strongly inhibits CYP2C19 bioactivation of clopidogrel to its active metabolite reducing antiplatelet protection.
management: Avoid omeprazole with clopidogrel. Consider pantoprazole or an H2 blocker as an alternative gastroprotective agent.

mechanism: Combined serotonergic activity increases the risk of life-threatening serotonin syndrome and lowers seizure threshold.
management: Avoid combination if possible. If required monitor closely for tremor rigidity hyperthermia and autonomic instability.

mechanism: Concomitant opioid and benzodiazepine therapy produces additive CNS and respiratory depression sedation and coma risk.
management: Limit dosages and durations to the minimum required. Counsel patient on severe sedation and respiratory depression signs.

mechanism: Additive negative inotropic chronotropic and dromotropic effects can precipitate severe bradycardia heart block or heart failure.
management: Avoid coadministration particularly in patients with impaired ventricular function or cardiac conduction defects.

mechanism: Synergistic inhibition of AV nodal conduction and myocardial contractility can induce severe bradycardia and hypotension.
management: Avoid concurrent use unless strictly supervised. Monitor ECG heart rate and blood pressure regularly.

mechanism: Dual non-dihydropyridine CCB and non-selective beta blocker therapy severely suppresses AV node conduction and cardiac output.
management: Avoid concurrent oral administration. Monitor pulse and hemodynamic stability if combination is unavoidable.

mechanism: Verapamil reduces renal and non-renal clearance of digoxin via P-glycoprotein inhibition increasing digoxin toxicity risk.
management: Reduce digoxin dose by 30-50% when starting verapamil. Monitor serum digoxin concentrations and cardiac rhythm closely.

mechanism: Concurrent ACE inhibition and potassium-sparing aldosterone antagonism creates severe risk of life-threatening hyperkalemia.
management: Monitor serum potassium and renal function within 1 week of initiation and regularly thereafter; avoid potassium supplements.

mechanism: Macrolide-induced gut flora alteration and potential CYP interaction can enhance warfarin anticoagulant effects.
management: Monitor INR carefully upon starting and stopping azithromycin; adjust warfarin dosage if INR rises.

mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 and alters intestinal flora leading to increased warfarin activity and elevated bleeding risk.
management: Monitor prothrombin time and INR closely during antimicrobial course and adjust warfarin dosage accordingly.

mechanism: Ibuprofen competitively interferes with irreversible platelet COX-1 inhibition by low-dose aspirin reducing cardioprotection.
management: Take immediate-release aspirin at least 30 minutes before or 8 hours after ibuprofen dose to preserve antiplatelet effect.

mechanism: Concomitant use increases upper gastrointestinal mucosal irritation and bleeding risk compared to either agent alone.
management: Avoid co-therapy where possible; if required co-prescribe a gastroprotective PPI and monitor for gastrointestinal toxicity.

mechanism: NSAID inhibition of renal prostaglandins attenuates losartan antihypertensive efficacy and may precipitate acute renal impairment.
management: Monitor blood pressure and renal parameters periodically; ensure adequate hydration during concurrent NSAID use.

mechanism: NSAIDs decrease renal blood flow via prostaglandin inhibition reducing telmisartan blood pressure control and straining kidneys.
management: Monitor blood pressure and serum creatinine; keep NSAID therapy at the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration.

mechanism: NSAIDs blunt the antihypertensive response of enalapril and compound the risk of renal deterioration in vulnerable patients.
management: Check renal function and potassium; titrate antihypertensive therapy and limit NSAID duration.

mechanism: Amlodipine moderately inhibits CYP3A4-mediated clearance of simvastatin increasing systemic statin exposure and myopathy risk.
management: Cap simvastatin daily dose at 20 mg when co-prescribed with amlodipine per clinical guidelines to mitigate myopathy risk.

mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inhibition by clarithromycin increases atorvastatin plasma concentrations elevating myopathy risk.
management: Limit atorvastatin dose to 20 mg daily during clarithromycin treatment or temporarily withhold the statin.

mechanism: Divalent calcium cations chelate ciprofloxacin in the gastrointestinal tract significantly impairing quinolone absorption.
management: Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium carbonate ingestion to avoid malabsorption.

mechanism: Calcium carbonate binds levothyroxine in the acidic gastric environment forming insoluble chelates and blunting absorption.
management: Separate administration of levothyroxine and calcium carbonate by at least 4 hours to preserve thyroid hormone absorption.

mechanism: Dual antiplatelet inhibition provides synergistic antithrombotic efficacy but significantly increases major bleed risk.
management: Use dual antiplatelet therapy only when clinically indicated with defined duration; monitor for hemorrhagic complications.

mechanism: NSAIDs decrease renal perfusion and competitively inhibit tubular methotrexate excretion causing serious methotrexate toxicity.
management: Exercise caution with low-dose methotrexate; monitor complete blood counts and renal function closely; avoid with high doses.

mechanism: Loop diuretic-induced hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia sensitize cardiac tissue drastically potentiating digoxin arrhythmias.
management: Monitor serum potassium magnesium and digoxin levels; maintain normokalemia through potassium replacement if needed.

mechanism: Dual blockade of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone axis impairs potassium excretion increasing risk of hyperkalemia.
management: Regularly assess serum potassium and creatinine; avoid concomitant potassium supplementation or salt substitutes.

mechanism: High prolonged doses of paracetamol (>2 g/day for several days) may inhibit warfarin metabolism and modestly raise INR.
management: Occasional therapeutic paracetamol use is generally safe; monitor INR if taking maximum therapeutic doses for >3 days.
